criteria.criterion: The build configuration and target documentation identify NUCLEO-G431RB as the firmware target, and the recorded target test uses that board.
criteria.observable: MCU/board target configuration and target test record
preconditions: Board assembled per Target Hardware.
procedure: Inspect the project target configuration and build output metadata.
Inspect the recorded target test setup and confirm it identifies NUCLEO-G431RB.
criteria.expected: The target is identified as NUCLEO-G431RB in both the build configuration and the target test record.

criteria.criterion: The motor-driver board listed in the hardware configuration and test setup is X-NUCLEO-IHM16M1 populated with the STSPIN830.
criteria.observable: Hardware bill of materials, board markings, and test setup record
preconditions: Board assembled per Target Hardware.
procedure: Inspect the hardware bill of materials and board markings.
Inspect the test setup record for the installed motor-driver board.
criteria.expected: The installed and documented motor-driver board is X-NUCLEO-IHM16M1 with an STSPIN830.

criteria.criterion: The motor identified in the test setup and documentation is GBM2804H-100T and its configured pole-pair count is 7.
criteria.observable: Motor label, motor configuration parameter, and test documentation
preconditions: Firmware tested on GBM2804H-100T.
procedure: Inspect the motor label and test setup documentation.
Inspect the firmware motor configuration for the pole-pair parameter.
criteria.expected: The motor model is GBM2804H-100T and the pole-pair parameter equals 7.

criteria.criterion: The documented laboratory supply setting for the system is 12 V DC.
criteria.observable: Laboratory power-supply display or setup record
preconditions: External supply provided.
procedure: Inspect the connected laboratory supply setting or its setup record.
Confirm the voltage and supply type.
criteria.expected: The supply is DC and its set voltage is 12 V.

criteria.criterion: When a run command is applied, PWM activity is observable on each of the U, V, and W motor outputs.
criteria.observable: Oscilloscope traces on the U, V, and W motor-driver outputs
preconditions: Motor connected to U, V, W outputs.
The motor-driver board and inverter are powered.
The firmware is in a run-command state with no active motor-control fault.
procedure: Connect oscilloscope channels to the U, V, and W outputs relative to the appropriate measurement reference.
Apply a motor run command.
Capture all three output waveforms during the commanded run.
criteria.expected: Each of U, V, and W has a continuous PWM waveform during the commanded run.

criteria.criterion: When a motor-control fault is injected or detected, the U, V, and W drive outputs are disabled.
criteria.observable: U, V, and W output levels or PWM duty after fault detection
preconditions: Motor connected to U, V, and W outputs.
The inverter is powered and producing PWM before the fault.
A controllable motor-control fault condition is available.
procedure: Start the motor command and verify PWM is present on U, V, and W.
Inject or trigger the specified motor-control fault.
Observe the three outputs after fault handling completes.
criteria.expected: PWM is disabled on U, V, and W after the fault is detected.
criteria.rationale: The requirement's failure behavior explicitly requires disabling outputs on any motor-control fault; this criterion makes that safety action observable at the three phase outputs.

criteria.criterion: During motor operation, the firmware reports phase-current samples from the IHM16M1 three-shunt sensing network, and the reported samples vary when motor load or phase conduction changes.
criteria.observable: Firmware phase-current sample values and their ADC input connections
preconditions: IHM16M1 is assembled with its three shunt networks.
The shunt-sense outputs are connected to the configured ADC inputs.
The motor is operating under a controllable load.
procedure: Start the motor at a safe operating point and record the firmware's phase-current samples.
Change the motor load or operating phase conditions.
Record the samples again and correlate the ADC inputs with the IHM16M1 shunt-sense outputs.
criteria.expected: The samples are sourced from the three-shunt ADC channels and at least one phase-current sample changes when load or phase conduction changes.

criteria.criterion: When phase-current sensing is made unavailable, the motor-drive outputs are disabled.
criteria.observable: PWM or gate-drive signals after ADC/current-sensing failure
preconditions: The motor is commanded to run and drive outputs are active.
The IHM16M1 shunt-sense signals are connected before the fault.
A controllable loss or invalidation of the current-sensing path is available.
procedure: Run the motor and verify active drive signals.
Disconnect or invalidate the configured current-sensing path.
Observe the motor-drive outputs after the sensing fault is detected.
criteria.expected: Motor-drive PWM is disabled after current sensing becomes unavailable.
criteria.rationale: The failure behavior explicitly requires disabling motor drive when sensing is unavailable; observing the drive outputs verifies the required safety response.

criteria.criterion: The firmware's three-phase drive implementation selects MCU hardware PWM peripherals rather than software-toggled GPIO timing.
criteria.observable: PWM peripheral initialization, channel configuration, and output-routing code
preconditions: PWM outputs are routed to the motor-driver inputs.
procedure: Inspect the three-phase drive initialization and update code.
Identify the configured MCU timer/PWM peripheral channels and their output pins.
Confirm that the phase duty updates write PWM peripheral compare registers rather than scheduling GPIO transitions.
criteria.expected: All three inverter phases are assigned to MCU hardware PWM channels, with duty controlled through PWM peripheral registers.

criteria.criterion: During steady motor operation, the three inverter PWM waveforms remain continuously hardware-timed without observable CPU-jitter artifacts.
criteria.observable: Oscilloscope capture of the three PWM output waveforms
preconditions: PWM outputs are routed to the motor-driver inputs.
The MCU firmware is running the motor-control loop.
The inverter is commanded to produce PWM.
procedure: Probe the three inverter PWM outputs with an oscilloscope.
Capture a sufficiently long interval during steady motor operation while the CPU performs normal firmware work.
Inspect pulse timing and edge placement across the capture.
criteria.expected: PWM pulses remain present for the full capture and their period and edge timing remain hardware-timed without missing pulses or observable CPU-scheduling jitter artifacts.

criteria.criterion: When a detected inverter or motor-control fault occurs, the hardware PWM outputs are disabled.
criteria.observable: Three-phase PWM output signals after fault detection
preconditions: The inverter is producing PWM before the fault.
A controllable fault condition recognized by the firmware is available.
procedure: Start PWM generation and verify output activity.
Trigger the detected fault condition.
Observe the three PWM outputs after the fault response.
criteria.expected: PWM output is disabled on all three inverter phases after fault detection.
criteria.rationale: The requirement's failure behavior requires PWM shutdown on a detected fault; checking all three outputs verifies that the hardware PWM safety action is applied to the complete inverter.

criteria.criterion: The motor operates under closed-loop sensorless FOC with valid commutation and torque control throughout the specified speed range.
criteria.observable: Phase-current waveforms, estimated rotor angle/speed, and measured motor response while commanded speed and load are varied.
preconditions: Target hardware is assembled.
Three-phase motor is connected.
The specified speed range and safe operating limits are configured.
procedure: Power the target and start the motor under speed control.
Command operating points spanning the specified speed range.
Observe phase currents and the sensorless estimator while applying representative torque demand.
Record whether commutation remains synchronized and torque follows the command at each operating point.
criteria.expected: Closed-loop sensorless commutation remains synchronized and commanded torque is controlled at every tested speed in the specified range.

criteria.criterion: A failed-to-converge sensorless observer causes the motor drive to be disabled.
criteria.observable: Observer convergence/fault status and the three PWM outputs after inducing or simulating estimator non-convergence.
preconditions: The motor and target are connected.
A test condition is available that causes the observer/estimator to fail to converge.
procedure: Start the motor or enter the estimator-active state.
Apply the estimator non-convergence condition.
Observe the estimator status and PWM outputs.
criteria.expected: An estimator failure is indicated and all motor-drive PWM outputs are disabled.
criteria.rationale: The requirement explicitly specifies the failure behavior when the observer/estimator does not converge; the criterion checks both the failure indication and the required safety action.

criteria.criterion: Immediately after power-on or reset, before any START command, the motor is stationary and all motor PWM outputs are disabled.
criteria.observable: Motor shaft motion and the three-phase PWM output signals before a START command is issued.
preconditions: The system has just been powered on or reset.
No START command has been sent.
procedure: Power on or reset the target.
Do not send any motor command.
Observe the shaft and measure all three PWM outputs during initialization and the pre-command interval.
criteria.expected: The shaft does not rotate and all motor PWM outputs remain disabled until START is received.

criteria.criterion: The measured shaft rotation direction matches each commanded direction for both CW and CCW commands.
criteria.observable: Measured shaft direction after issuing CW and CCW direction commands.
preconditions: The motor is connected and free to rotate.
The system is in a state that accepts START and direction commands.
procedure: Start the motor with a CW direction command and measure shaft direction.
Stop the motor using the normal stop procedure.
Start the motor with a CCW direction command and measure shaft direction.
criteria.expected: The first run rotates clockwise and the second run rotates counter-clockwise, with no direction-command mismatch.

criteria.criterion: A valid SPEED command issued during running changes the motor to the new target speed without entering the stopped state.
criteria.observable: Motor state, measured speed, and speed-command/status values during an in-run speed change.
preconditions: The motor is running under speed control.
The new SPEED command is within the allowed range.
procedure: Start the motor and wait for steady running.
Issue a new valid SPEED command without issuing STOP.
Record the motor state and speed throughout the transition.
criteria.expected: The commanded speed changes to the new value, the motor remains in the run state throughout the transition, and no stop state occurs between the two speeds.

criteria.criterion: A running CW motor commanded to reverse decelerates through zero before any reverse torque is applied and then accelerates CCW.
criteria.observable: Measured signed speed, phase current/torque direction, and motor state after a DIR CCW command.
preconditions: The motor is running CW at a steady speed within the specified operating range.
Speed and torque direction can be measured.
procedure: Run the motor steadily in the CW direction.
Issue DIR CCW while the motor is running.
Capture signed speed and torque direction from the command through reversal.
criteria.expected: Signed speed reaches 0 RPM before torque changes to the CCW direction; the motor subsequently accelerates CCW, and no reverse-torque spike occurs before the zero-speed crossing.

criteria.criterion: If the controller cannot complete the commanded reversal sequence, it rejects the direction change and continues operating in the current direction.
criteria.observable: Direction-command result, motor direction, and controller status when reversal sequencing is made impossible.
preconditions: The motor is running in a known direction.
A test condition is present that prevents completion of the controlled reversal sequence.
procedure: Issue a direction command for the opposite direction.
Observe the command result, status, and measured motor direction.
criteria.expected: The opposite-direction command is refused and the motor remains in its original direction.
criteria.rationale: The failure behavior requires refusal rather than an unsafe partial reversal when the required sequencing cannot be achieved.

criteria.criterion: When startup is prevented, the controller aborts within the configured maximum startup time or attempt count, disables PWM, and reports a startup fault in STATUS.
criteria.observable: Elapsed startup time or attempt counter, three-phase PWM outputs, and STATUS fault field after a failed MOTOR START.
preconditions: The motor is at standstill.
Operating limits are configured.
A rotor lock, extreme load, or other controlled condition prevents startup.
procedure: Apply the startup-preventing condition.
Issue MOTOR START.
Measure elapsed time and/or count startup attempts until the controller aborts.
Read STATUS and measure the PWM outputs.
criteria.expected: The abort occurs no later than the configured maximum startup time or attempt count; STATUS indicates a startup fault and all PWM outputs are disabled.

criteria.criterion: After a startup fault, the drive remains disabled until the fault is cleared and a new START command is issued.
criteria.observable: Latched fault status, PWM outputs, and motor state after fault, clear, and restart commands.
preconditions: A startup fault has been induced and reported.
The motor is at standstill.
procedure: After the startup fault, verify that no START command is sent and observe PWM and STATUS.
Clear the fault without issuing START and observe again.
Issue a new START command under valid startup conditions.
criteria.expected: The fault remains latched and PWM remains disabled before clear plus new START; only after both actions may the drive leave the fault-disabled state.
criteria.rationale: The stated postcondition defines a latched fault and requires both fault clearing and a new START before another startup attempt.

criteria.criterion: Every startup attempt in a representative series reaches the running state and sustained rotation without manual intervention or a fault.
criteria.observable: Motor state, measured rotation, and fault status for each startup attempt.
preconditions: The motor is at standstill.
The motor, supply, and parameters are within configured operating limits.
procedure: Perform the defined series of startup attempts from standstill.
For each attempt, issue START and observe until the controller reports running.
Check sustained rotation and fault status without intervening commands.
criteria.expected: Each attempt reaches the running state with sustained rotation, no manual intervention, and no fault indication.

criteria.criterion: With a fixed SPEED command and constant load, the motor remains synchronized and STATUS reports an approximately constant estimated speed throughout the observation interval.
criteria.observable: Motor rotation, synchronism, fixed SPEED command, and STATUS estimated-speed samples over the observation interval.
preconditions: The motor is running within operating limits.
A fixed SPEED command is active.
The mechanical load is constant.
procedure: Start the motor and apply a fixed SPEED command.
Wait for the running condition to establish.
Observe motor synchronism and record STATUS estimated speed over the defined observation interval.
criteria.expected: No loss of synchronism occurs and the STATUS estimated-speed samples remain approximately constant for the full observation interval.

criteria.criterion: A stop command decelerates the motor to standstill without oscillation or reverse kick and leaves the drive disabled.
criteria.observable: Measured signed speed, shaft behavior, motor state, and PWM outputs after STOP.
preconditions: The motor is running.
The motor and supply are within operating limits.
procedure: Run the motor at a representative speed.
Issue the stop command.
Measure signed speed and observe shaft behavior through standstill, then measure PWM outputs and read motor state.
criteria.expected: Speed decreases to 0 RPM, no uncontrolled oscillation or reverse kick is observed, the motor is stopped, and all drive PWM outputs are disabled.

criteria.criterion: Project artifacts contain the final speed, startup, and current tuning parameters together with validation results for the actual motor and supply, dated or otherwise attributable before extended runtime testing.
criteria.observable: Committed configuration/tuning artifacts and the motor-and-supply validation report or equivalent recorded test results.
preconditions: The actual motor and supply are identified.
Project and validation artifacts are available for inspection.
procedure: Inspect the final firmware configuration and tuning records.
Verify that speed, startup, and current limits are recorded.
Inspect the validation results for the identified motor and supply and their timing relative to extended runtime testing.
criteria.expected: All three limit groups have recorded final values, the records identify the actual motor and supply, validation results are present, and the validation predates extended runtime testing.

criteria.criterion: The UART configuration in the firmware build is set to 115200 baud with 8 data bits, no parity, and 1 stop bit.
criteria.observable: UART peripheral configuration in source and generated build configuration
preconditions: The NUCLEO-G431RB firmware configuration and build artifacts are available.
procedure: Inspect the UART initialization code and target configuration.
Confirm the baud rate and frame-format fields.
criteria.expected: 115200 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, and 1 stop bit (8-N-1).

criteria.criterion: A terminal or UART loopback exchanges command and response data successfully using the configured interface.
criteria.observable: Received UART bytes in the terminal or loopback capture
preconditions: The firmware is running on the NUCLEO-G431RB.
A host is connected to the UART pins.
The host terminal is configured for 115200 8-N-1.
procedure: Open the host terminal at 115200 8-N-1.
Transmit a supported command such as STATUS.
Capture the UART response.
criteria.expected: The transmitted command is received by the firmware and a valid response is received without framing or communication errors.

criteria.criterion: A valid MOTOR START command causes the motor to rotate and the subsequent STATUS response to report the run state.
criteria.observable: Motor shaft motion and STATUS state field
preconditions: The firmware is initialized.
The motor is stopped.
A valid direction and speed are configured.
Start safety conditions are satisfied.
The UART link is established.
procedure: Send the exact command MOTOR START over UART.
Observe the motor shaft.
Send STATUS over UART and parse the system-state field.
criteria.expected: The motor is rotating and STATUS reports RUN or the project-defined equivalent run state.

criteria.criterion: A MOTOR START command issued while a stated start-safety condition is violated does not start the motor.
criteria.observable: Motor motion and reported system state after the rejected command
preconditions: The firmware is initialized.
The motor is stopped.
At least one configured start-safety condition is deliberately violated.
The UART link is established.
procedure: Send MOTOR START over UART.
Observe the motor and query STATUS.
criteria.expected: The motor remains stopped and the system does not enter RUN; the response/state indicates the project-defined safety refusal or fault behavior.

criteria.criterion: A MOTOR STOP command issued while the motor is running leaves the motor stationary and disables the PWM outputs at the end of the stop sequence.
criteria.observable: Motor shaft motion and PWM output signals after stop completion
preconditions: The motor is running.
The UART link is established.
A logic analyzer or oscilloscope is connected to the PWM outputs.
procedure: Send the exact command MOTOR STOP over UART.
Wait until the stop sequence completes.
Observe the motor and measure the PWM outputs.
criteria.expected: The shaft is stationary and all motor-drive PWM outputs are disabled after the stop sequence completes.

criteria.criterion: SPEED commands for 300 RPM, 1000 RPM, and a valid intermediate RPM update the target-speed field to the commanded value.
criteria.observable: Target-speed field in STATUS responses
preconditions: The system is initialized.
The UART link is established.
The motor may be stopped or running.
procedure: Send SPEED 300 and query STATUS.
Send SPEED 1000 and query STATUS.
Send SPEED with a valid intermediate value and query STATUS.
Parse the target-speed field after each command.
criteria.expected: The reported target speeds are respectively 300 RPM, 1000 RPM, and exactly the commanded intermediate value.

criteria.criterion: A DIR CW command causes the commanded direction field to become CW and subsequent motor rotation to be clockwise.
criteria.observable: STATUS direction field and motor rotation direction
preconditions: The system is initialized.
The motor can be started safely.
The UART link is established.
procedure: Send DIR CW over UART.
Query STATUS and inspect the direction field.
Start the motor if it is stopped.
Observe the rotation direction.
criteria.expected: STATUS reports direction=CW and the motor rotates clockwise.

criteria.criterion: A DIR CCW command causes the commanded direction field to become CCW and subsequent motor rotation to be counter-clockwise.
criteria.observable: STATUS direction field and motor rotation direction
preconditions: The system is initialized.
The motor can be started safely.
The UART link is established.
procedure: Send DIR CCW over UART.
Query STATUS and inspect the direction field.
Start the motor if it is stopped.
Observe the rotation direction.
criteria.expected: STATUS reports direction=CCW and the motor rotates counter-clockwise.

criteria.criterion: Sending STATUS over an established UART link produces a response payload containing the system state, target speed, estimated actual speed, commanded direction, and fault status fields.
criteria.observable: STATUS response payload
preconditions: The firmware is running.
The UART link is established.
The system has reached a known initialized state.
procedure: Send the exact command STATUS over UART.
Capture the complete response payload.
Parse the response for the required field names and values.
criteria.expected: One response payload is received and contains fields for state, target speed, estimated actual speed, direction, and fault status.
criteria.rationale: The requirement requires all required status fields, and DIAG-001 through DIAG-005 define the fields that STATUS must provide.

criteria.criterion: Each unknown, malformed, or truncated UART command leaves the system state, target speed, direction, and fault status identical to their values before the command.
criteria.observable: STATUS snapshots taken before and after invalid UART inputs
preconditions: The UART link is established.
The system is in a known STOPPED or RUN state.
The target speed, direction, and fault status can be reported by STATUS.
procedure: Query STATUS and record state, target speed, direction, and fault status.
Send STAR, SPEED 42a, and a truncated command frame individually.
Query STATUS after each invalid input.
Compare every recorded field with its corresponding pre-command value.
criteria.expected: For every invalid input, state, target speed, direction, and fault status are unchanged.

criteria.criterion: SPEED 200 and SPEED 1100 are rejected without changing the previously valid target speed or system state.
criteria.observable: Target-speed and system-state fields in STATUS responses
preconditions: The system is initialized.
The UART link is established.
A valid target speed has already been set.
The system is in a known state.
procedure: Query STATUS and record the target speed and system state.
Send SPEED 200 and query STATUS.
Restore or verify the same valid baseline if needed.
Send SPEED 1100 and query STATUS.
Compare the results with the baseline.
criteria.expected: After each out-of-range command, the target speed equals the prior valid value and the system state is unchanged.

criteria.criterion: The STATUS response contains a state field whose value unambiguously identifies the current system state.
criteria.observable: State field in the STATUS response
preconditions: The system is in a known state.
The UART link is established.
procedure: Place the system in a known state such as INIT, STOPPED, RUN, or FAULT.
Send STATUS.
Parse the state field.
criteria.expected: The response contains a non-ambiguous state value matching the actual state, such as INIT, STOPPED, RUN, or FAULT.

criteria.criterion: The target-speed field in STATUS equals the most recently commanded valid target speed.
criteria.observable: Numeric target-speed field in the STATUS response
preconditions: The system is initialized.
The UART link is established.
A valid target speed in the range 300–1000 RPM has been commanded.
procedure: Send a valid SPEED command.
Send STATUS.
Parse the numeric target-speed field.
criteria.expected: The field is numeric and equals the commanded value in RPM, within the inclusive range 300–1000 RPM.

criteria.criterion: The STATUS response contains a numeric estimated-actual-speed field expressed in RPM.
criteria.observable: Estimated actual-speed field in the STATUS response
preconditions: The firmware is running.
The UART link is established.
procedure: Send STATUS.
Parse the estimated actual-speed field.
criteria.expected: The response contains a parseable numeric value representing estimated speed in RPM at the query time.

criteria.criterion: The direction field in STATUS is either CW or CCW and matches the most recent DIR command.
criteria.observable: Direction field in the STATUS response
preconditions: The system is initialized.
The UART link is established.
procedure: Send DIR CW and query STATUS.
Send DIR CCW and query STATUS.
criteria.expected: The direction field reports CW after DIR CW and CCW after DIR CCW.

criteria.criterion: The STATUS response contains a fault-status field that changes to the faulted indication when a known fault is induced.
criteria.observable: Fault-status field in STATUS before and during an induced fault
preconditions: Fault detection is implemented.
The UART link is established.
A representative fault can be safely induced.
procedure: Query STATUS with no active fault and record the fault-status field.
Induce a known fault.
Query STATUS again.
Compare the reported fault status with the induced condition.
criteria.expected: The response contains a fault-status field, and during the induced fault it indicates that a fault is present.

criteria.criterion: When each representative fault is active, STATUS reports a non-null fault code matching that fault category.
criteria.observable: Fault-code field in STATUS during induced undervoltage, overcurrent, current-sense, and startup-timeout faults
preconditions: STATUS is available.
The fault-inducing test setup is prepared.
Each representative fault can be induced safely and independently.
procedure: Induce an undervoltage-limit fault and query STATUS.
Induce an overcurrent-limit fault and query STATUS.
Induce a current-sense fault and query STATUS.
Induce a startup-timeout fault and query STATUS.
Record the fault code for each condition.
criteria.expected: Each STATUS response contains a non-null code, and the codes identify respectively undervoltage-limit, overcurrent-limit, current-sense, and startup-failure categories.

categories.name: Drive Safety, Fault Handling & Reset Protection

criteria.criterion: Measured steady-state and transient phase RMS motor current remains at or below the configured maximum, with the configured maximum no greater than 1.5 A RMS unless a lower validated project limit is configured.
criteria.observable: Phase-current measurement RMS value and configured current-limit value during steady-state operation and specified speed transients
preconditions: Current sensing is operational.
A maximum RMS current limit is configured.
The motor is operating in steady state and through the specified speed transients.
procedure: Record the configured RMS current limit.
Run the motor at steady state over the applicable operating range.
Apply the specified speed transients while recording phase current.
Calculate or read the measured phase RMS current and compare each value with the configured limit.
criteria.expected: For every recorded interval, measured phase RMS current is <= the configured limit; the configured limit is <=1.5 A RMS unless a lower validated limit is explicitly configured.

criteria.criterion: When a detectable motor-driver fault is asserted while the motor is running, all inverter PWM outputs enter the disabled state and produce no subsequent drive pulses.
criteria.observable: Inverter PWM output signals after motor-driver fault assertion
preconditions: The motor is running.
The motor-driver fault input or condition is detectable by the firmware.
PWM outputs are enabled before the fault is asserted.
A means of observing all inverter PWM outputs is connected.
procedure: Start the motor and confirm that PWM pulses are present.
Assert the motor-driver fault condition.
Capture all PWM outputs from the instant of fault assertion onward.
Check the output state and pulse count after the assertion.
criteria.expected: PWM outputs transition to the disabled state and no drive pulse occurs after the fault assertion.

criteria.criterion: After a motor-control fault disables PWM, the firmware remains in the disabled condition until the fault is cleared and a new START command is received.
criteria.observable: PWM-enable state and motor-control state after fault clear without and with a new START command
preconditions: The motor is running and PWM has been disabled by a motor-control fault.
The fault can be cleared and a START command can be issued.
procedure: Clear the motor-control fault without issuing START.
Inspect the PWM-enable state and motor-control state.
Issue a new START command.
Inspect the PWM-enable state again.
criteria.expected: PWM remains disabled before the new START command and may be enabled only after the fault is cleared and the new START command is received.
criteria.rationale: The requirement's failure behavior specifies that the drive remains disabled until both fault clearance and a new START command; this criterion checks both parts of that recovery gate.

criteria.criterion: An attempted start or continued run with either a configured voltage-limit violation or a configured current-limit violation results in drive inhibition or automatic stop with PWM disabled.
criteria.observable: START result, motor-running state, PWM outputs, and reported fault status while voltage or current is outside its configured limit
preconditions: Voltage and current limits are configured.
Voltage and current violation conditions can be generated or applied safely.
The firmware can detect both violation types.
procedure: Apply a voltage condition outside the configured voltage limits and attempt to start the motor; record the START result and PWM state.
Run the motor, then apply a current condition outside the configured current limits; record the motor state and PWM state.
Repeat as needed for each supported lower- and upper-limit violation.
criteria.expected: For every out-of-limit condition, START is refused or an already-running motor is stopped, PWM is disabled, and fault status is reported.

criteria.criterion: A START command issued while measured DC supply voltage is below the configured minimum or above the configured maximum is refused and leaves the drive disabled.
criteria.observable: START response, PWM-enable state, and measured DC voltage at the time of the command
preconditions: Minimum and maximum DC voltage thresholds are configured.
DC supply voltage measurement is operational.
The supply can be safely set below the minimum and above the maximum.
procedure: Set the DC supply below the configured minimum and verify the measured value is out of range.
Issue START and record the command response and PWM state.
Set the DC supply above the configured maximum and repeat the START test.
criteria.expected: For both below-minimum and above-maximum conditions, START is refused and PWM remains disabled.

criteria.criterion: When the measured DC supply voltage crosses either configured threshold while the motor is running, the drive is disabled and STATUS indicates a fault.
criteria.observable: DC supply voltage crossing, inverter PWM outputs, motor-running state, and STATUS value
preconditions: The motor is running with PWM enabled.
Minimum and maximum DC voltage thresholds are configured.
DC supply voltage measurement and STATUS reporting are operational.
procedure: Run the motor within the configured voltage range.
Change the DC supply below the minimum and record the voltage crossing, PWM state, and STATUS.
Restore the supply to the valid range, restart the motor, then change the supply above the maximum and repeat.
criteria.expected: For each threshold crossing, PWM is disabled, the motor is no longer driven, and STATUS indicates a fault.

criteria.criterion: After a voltage-limit shutdown, the drive remains disabled while the measured voltage is out of range and does not restart until the voltage is valid and a new START command is received.
criteria.observable: PWM-enable state and motor-control state after voltage recovery, before and after a new START command
preconditions: The motor has been stopped by an out-of-range DC supply voltage.
The supply can be returned to the configured valid range.
procedure: Keep the supply out of range and verify PWM remains disabled.
Return the supply to the valid range without issuing START and verify PWM remains disabled.
Issue a new START command and inspect the drive state.
criteria.expected: PWM remains disabled while voltage is out of range and after voltage recovery without START; it can resume only after valid voltage and a new START command.
criteria.rationale: The failure behavior states that the drive remains disabled until voltage returns within range and a new START is issued; the criterion verifies that recovery does not occur automatically.

criteria.criterion: While running closed-loop control, inducing a phase-current sensing disconnection, ADC rail or saturation value, or ADC-DMA disable causes PWM to be disabled with no subsequent drive pulses and STATUS to indicate a faulted state.
criteria.observable: Phase-current sensor or ADC condition, inverter PWM outputs, and STATUS value after each induced sensor fault
preconditions: The motor is running under closed-loop control.
Phase-current sensing and ADC/DMA fault injection or equivalent test access is available.
PWM outputs and STATUS are observable.
procedure: Run the motor and confirm PWM activity and a non-fault STATUS.
Induce a phase-current shunt-signal disconnection, force an ADC reading to a rail or saturation value, and disable ADC DMA in separate test runs.
For each fault, capture PWM outputs from fault injection onward and read STATUS.
criteria.expected: For every induced sensor fault, PWM is disabled, no drive pulse occurs after fault detection/assertion, and STATUS indicates the FAULT state.

criteria.criterion: After a phase-current sensing fault is cleared, the firmware keeps the drive disabled until START is issued again.
criteria.observable: PWM-enable state and motor-control state after clearing the injected phase-current fault
preconditions: The motor has entered FAULT and PWM has been disabled because of a phase-current sensing fault.
The injected sensor fault can be cleared.
procedure: Clear the injected sensing fault without issuing START.
Inspect the motor-control state and PWM-enable state.
Issue START and inspect the states again.
criteria.expected: The system remains in FAULT or an equivalent non-driving state with PWM disabled before START, and does not resume driving until START is issued.
criteria.rationale: The requirement's failure behavior explicitly requires disabled operation until the fault is cleared and START is reissued; this checks the restart interlock.

criteria.criterion: Following an induced watchdog reset or brown-out while the motor is running, PWM outputs remain inactive during reset and after reboot until a new valid START command is received.
criteria.observable: Inverter PWM signals across the reset or brown-out event and after reboot
preconditions: The system is running and producing PWM before the reset test.
Watchdog reset and brown-out events can be induced safely.
PWM outputs can be observed continuously across reset and reboot.
procedure: Run the motor and confirm PWM activity.
Induce a watchdog reset and capture PWM through reset and reboot; do not issue START.
Repeat the capture for a brown-out event.
Issue a valid START command after initialization and inspect PWM again.
criteria.expected: No PWM activity is present during either reset or reboot, no PWM appears before the new valid START command, and PWM may resume only after initialization and START.

criteria.criterion: After either a watchdog reset or brown-out reboot, STATUS reports STOPPED before any new START command is received.
criteria.observable: STATUS value after reboot and before START
preconditions: A watchdog reset or brown-out has completed and firmware initialization has completed.
No START command has been issued after reboot.
procedure: Read STATUS immediately after the system is available following each reset type.
Do not issue START before reading STATUS.
criteria.expected: STATUS is STOPPED for both watchdog-reset and brown-out recovery before any START command.

criteria.criterion: A deliberate control-software hang while the motor is running causes the watchdog to reset the MCU, after which the motor remains stopped with PWM disabled until a new START command is received.
criteria.observable: Reset indication or reboot sequence, PWM outputs, motor state, and post-reboot START response
preconditions: The system is running with the watchdog enabled.
The control task can be deliberately prevented from servicing the watchdog.
PWM outputs and MCU reset or reboot indication are observable.
procedure: Start the motor and verify PWM activity.
Induce the deliberate software hang.
Observe the MCU reset or reboot and monitor PWM through and after the reset.
After reboot, verify the motor remains stopped and issue no START.
Issue a new START command and observe the resulting drive state.
criteria.expected: The MCU resets after the control software stops servicing the watchdog; PWM is disabled after reset, the motor remains stopped before START, and a new START is required before operation resumes.
